How it's calculated: Total no resets = product of every multiplier (× qty). Total = Total no resetsresetters + 1, one full pass per reset. Total Length = Σ length × qty + extra length (one pass). MPU = (Total no resets)1 / Total Length, which equals Total1 / (length × passes), so resetting does not change MPU.

21 – – –
Rates
Progress & Cash

How it's calculated: each rebirth gives skips + 1 lives (20 skips = 21 lives). Rebirths per hour = 3600 ÷ speed, and lives per hour = rebirths per hour × lives per rebirth. Every skip multiplies the cash you need by 1,000, so 20 skips need price × 1060. When the price field is blank, it is estimated from the life ranges in the MPU site's suffix list: the price climbs smoothly through each suffix's life range and is capped at 10 NVSPTGNTL (10241) from life 80,351. Time to target assumes every rebirth takes the same number of seconds.

Price Rules
PlatformStart+ per buyfor firstthen +
⚠ = not confirmed on the wiki; edit it if your shop shows otherwise

How it's calculated: each purchase raises the price of the next platform of that type. With k already owned, the next price is Start + (+ per buy) × min(k, first) + (then +) × max(0, k − first), and the cost of buying several is the sum of those prices. Small Platforms are sold by The Masked Man for a random 117–221 uC and don't scale. Shards per rebirth defaults to ⌊skips ÷ 2⌋ using the Rebirth tab's skips (1 Shard of Life per 2 lives skipped), and the time to earn the shards uses that tab's speed.

Sources: Category:Platform, Hydraulic Standard Platform, Small Platform, NamuWiki tips (shards per skip)

Options

How it builds: cash needed = rebirth price × 1,000skips, and ore value = ore base value × furnace × resetters × everything in your lines × blasters & portables (the MPU site's model). Your setup is a row of lines: give each one a length in units and choose the resetter at its end (Auto uses the strongest resetters you've marked). The ore goes through Line 1, its resetter, Line 2, and so on, then into the furnace. An item only upgrades the ore once per reset cycle, so the same item twice before a resetter doesn't count (it's flagged), and each copy in a line needs a copy you own. Add items by hand with + Add item, or press ⚡ Auto build to fill the lines from the items you've marked as owned: it uses the best multiplier-per-unit items first, fits each one into the line with the least space left, drops anything the target doesn't need, and can keep your manual picks or rebuild every line. "N Resetters" states and entries that already count extra Midas uses aren't offered, because lines, shields and blasters are worked out here instead. Many items have conditions (wet ore, Havium, other items required): check each line's Conditions column.

Midas, Void Drive & portables: each blaster use has a death roll (Midas 1 in 3) that uses up a shield; with no shields left the ore dies. Your best owned blaster gets as many uses along your lines as keep survival at or above your target (MPU site default 60%, starting from 3 shields). Turtle Dignifier (+1) and Tortoise Fortifier (+3) add shields once per ore when they're in a line. With Void Drive on, a Void Drive line comes after your last line: Void Drive (×100) resets shields to 15, then very fast conveyors carry the ore past blasters along the sides and straight into the furnace before it dies 3 seconds later. The ore never loops back through resetters after Void Drive. Total survival = survival before Void Drive × survival after it × the chance of surviving risky portables (Methuselah's Mask 1 in 12 per use, Deceptive Sorcery and Doom Mortar 1 in 20). Portables get their per-tag uses once per reset cycle, once-per-ore portables count once, only your best pulsar is used, Ion Field is 2.5× then 1.8× per tag, and ghosts run Future → Past → Present with each earlier ghost doubling the next. Portables and blasters take no line length.

How to Redeem
  1. Join Miner's Haven on Roblox.
  2. Open Settings with the cog on the left side of the screen.
  3. Type or paste the code into the Enter Code box.
  4. Press Redeem.

Codes are case-sensitive and the punctuation matters (for example ElevenYears!!), so copy them with the buttons. Each code works once per account.

Cash Suffixes
#SuffixNameValueZerosRebirth price at livesOoftopian ×Notes

Each suffix is 1,000× the one before it. Suffixes are matched without caring about capitals in the converter, but the in-game names use the capitals shown. "Rebirth price at lives" shows which lives' rebirth price falls in that suffix; it's capped at 10 NVSPTGNTL from life 80,351. Ooftopian × is the Ooftopian Refiner's multiplier for ore worth that suffix (1.5× per suffix, capped at 150×). Data: the MPU site's suffix list.

How Superstitious Crafting Works
1. Unlock it. Do the Second Sacrifice, reach life S+1,000, then talk to Draedon in the Sporest (past John Doe's cave) to get the True Book of Knowledge.
2. Get a catalyst. Place the True Book of Knowledge and that catalyst's five items on your base and rebirth. About a 30–33% chance per rebirth to get the catalyst. These items are not used up, and other items on your base don't matter.
3. Craft at Draedon. Bring the catalyst to Draedon and add Reborn items until you reach the item's amount of six elements: Aether, Water, Earth, Fire, Order and Entropy. The catalyst and those reborns are used up. Shiny versions work too.
Catalysts: What to Put on Your Base

Tick the items you have to track how close you are. "How to get it" shows what each item is crafted from at The Craftsman.

Can I Salvage This?
Salvaging at The Craftsman

The Craftsman turns Reborn and Adv. Reborn items into Shards of Life: 27 − the item's rarity (rarity 19 = 8 shards, rarity 1 = 26 shards).

Rarity
Shards
  • Don't salvage Adv. Reborns.
  • Keep anything in a catalyst chain (see the list below), and check it isn't needed for an Evolved, Fusion or Enchanted item you want.
  • Superstitious items can be crafted from almost any Reborn as element fodder, so keep a stock of common reborns if you plan to craft lots of them.

Every item page on the Miner's Haven Wiki (). Multipliers are read from each item's effects text, so check the effects for conditions. Sizes are length × width × height in units. MPU = multiplier1 / length. Upgraders that weren't in your MPU data before were added to the Calculator and Setup Builder; items already there were left unchanged.

Ore Status Effects

Upgraders can give ore status effects. Most can be removed by Wild Spore, Deadly Spore, Azure Spore, The Death Cap and Resetting Devices. Effects marked Destroys ore will kill the ore if you don't deal with them.

Every Mystery Box

Avg boxes = how many boxes it takes on average to get one item of that tier (1 ÷ chance). For 90% = boxes for a 90% chance of at least one. Avg cost = average uC spent per item at Spook McDooks' price. Free boxes come from Research Crates, daily gifts, codes and rebirths, so real costs are often lower.

What You Can Unbox

Lucky Clovers (25 uC from Spook McDooks, or from Research Crates) don't raise the odds, but let a win give 2–3 copies of the item, for any tier including Vintages, Exotics and Relics. You can switch them off in the box menu. The spinning roulette is just for show: the item is already decided when you open the box. Source: Miner's Haven Wiki: Mystery Boxes.
